_about.purpose: Versioned Algolia synonyms, pushed by scripts/2-index.js. Never edited in the dashboard, for the same reason settings and rules are not: the configuration is part of the codebase, it gets reviewed in diffs, and a dashboard-only change is a change nobody can trace (CLAUDE.md §5).
contract_for_2-index.js: Push `synonyms` verbatim as the saveSynonyms payload, with replaceExistingSynonyms true so this file is the whole synonym set rather than an addition to whatever the dashboard holds.
Keys prefixed with `_` are documentation and must never be sent to Algolia.
Each synonym needs a stable, human-readable objectID. Algolia's synonym schema has no `description` field the way a rule does, so the id and this file are the only places the reasoning can live.
The file is optional. 2-index.js runs without it; it aborts on a file that exists but carries no `synonyms` array.

_rationale.the_ies_plurals: Four entries, all the same shape, all the same cause. `-y` to `-ies` puts the plural three edits from the corpus form — `wineries` against `winery` — past `minWordSizefor2Typos: 8`, so no typo threshold reaches them and three of the four returned zero results. Measured on the live index: `breweries` 0 to 9 hits, `wineries` 0 to 10, `eateries` 0 to 11, `bakeries` 1 to 3. Every other plural in the corpus vocabulary is already covered without a synonym, either by typo tolerance on a trailing `s` or by the `category-query-*` rules, whose `alternatives: true` makes `steakhouses` behave as `steakhouse`. See the test-queries.md change log.
_rationale.one_way_not_two: `oneWaySynonym` rather than a two-way pair, because the plural appears nowhere in the extract: `brewery` 8 times in a name plus 3 as a `cuisine_tag`, `winery` 10, `eatery` 11, `bakery` 2, and `breweries`, `wineries`, `eateries`, `bakeries` 0 times in any attribute. A two-way synonym would additionally declare that a singular query should reach the plural, which matches nothing and states something untrue of the data. Verified after the push: the four singular queries are byte-identical with synonyms on and off, so the direction does not leak.
_rationale.k12_deliberately_absent: `pappas brothers` gets no entry, though this file was long described as owed to it. That prediction was refuted on 2026-09-03: the query returns Pappas Bros. Steakhouse at rank 1 through `removeWordsIfNoResults`, which drops the unmatched last word, and test-queries.md K12 has carried a `pass` since. The 66 records with a period abbreviation — `Bros.`, `St.`, `Mt.`, in data/exploration.md A1.4 — may still deserve synonyms, but CLAUDE.md §8 forbids adding one before a case demands it.
